experiments.primary_claim: Distinguish control defects and nondeterminism from state-dependent contact failures.
Find physically useful, executable contact-phase corrections under full-task constraints.
Get well-trained same-authority residual RL, with full-cost baselines.
Isolate additional causal value of explicit action-effect feedback over equal-observation/history RL and strong planning.
After a reliable independent gain, test novel conditions, another contact mechanism and industrial adapter.

unresolved_questions: Matched LN failures never enter hold: native success occurs at154/161 but the stricter observed orientation threshold blocks termination. Can an observable, stable completion contract preserve success without privileged true-goal stopping?
Can task-conditioned restriction of legitimate skill parameters retain search successes without removing authority needed under real YZ/grasp variations?
Can persistent contact probes identify hidden task error beyond the same raw history and geometric search, with measurable information and control benefit?
Can a mature matched-authority RL baseline outperform progress search10/12 on new conditions rather than just weak SAC1/12?
How much residual failure is observed-goal early stopping or insufficient hold stability, rather than wrong contact action?
